entries.title: Karpathy session 0a60cb7ab847
entries.content:
## Delta

Both independent reviews came back **FAIL**, for the same reason. Nothing is CRITICAL or HIGH, and the fixes are in progress.

**The gap:** `/mcp` sessions, confirmations and confirm tokens are now tied to each signed-in person. AG-UI chat threads and their approval interrupts are still tied only to the shared principal (`console-ui`). Suppose two people were mapped to that principal with `/agui` routed, which is exactly what `lke-agent-settings` sets up. If B learned A's thread ID, B could:
- read A's chat history;
- approve or deny A's pending write;
- push A's idle chat out.

Today's live config isn't exposed: only `/auth/session` is routed, and there is one person.

**What else the reviews found:**
- **Closed:** the 8.1 security findings LOW-1, LOW-2, LOW-4 and LOW-5, and all ten 8.2 findings.
- **Not touched:** `/api/v0`, the gateway, the default CID recipe and `go.mod`.
- **Smaller issues:**
  - a false "keys expired" warning after a quiet period;
  - an unclear error for configs with a long `jwks_cache_ttl`;
  - the config doc row naming the wrong tests;
  - a contradiction in the `lke-agent-settings` proposal;
  - a few comment and wording nits.
- **Routes default:** narrowing it doesn't need the breaking-change `!` marker, because v0.44 hasn't been tagged.

Reports, saved verbatim:
- `.agent-team/kubo-ipfs-agentic/findings/security/agent-backend-settings/mcp-oidc-hardening-5.1-security-review.md`
- `.agent-team/kubo-ipfs-agentic/findings/review/agent-backend-settings/mcp-oidc-hardening-5.2-compat-review.md`

**Checkpoint:** `186525117`, pushed. Before committing I cleared two stale locks left from before the reboot: the single-writer lock and a git `index.lock`. Neither process was still running.

**Correction cycle (the one allowed), running in parallel:**
- **Engineer:**
  - ties AG-UI threads, interrupts and approvals (including the UAR backend) to each person;
  - makes sure one person can never push out another's chat;
  - adds a two-person `/agui` test through HTTP;
  - fixes the false warning and the error message.
- **Architect:**
  - corrects the changelog and ADR wording, the config doc's test list and the migration note;
  - fixes the `lke-agent-settings` contradiction and the small doc nits.

The spec requirement stays as written; the code is being brought up to it rather than the spec narrowed.

After both finish, I'll rerun the gate, with `-v` on the CLI tests this time so the log shows each test actually ran. Then I'll send the changes back to the same two reviewers for confirmation.

entries.content:
## Delta

<od-focus key="7477cc2db424a94d" open="index.html" show="index.html, DESIGN-PROPOSAL.md"/>

<od-done key="7477cc2db424a94d"/>

I ran the full loop (assess, analyze, plan, execute, reflect) as a child phase under Kubo's `agent-backend-settings`. It produced a clickable prototype, a design proposal and eight OpenSpec changes. Nothing was opened in a browser; the only checks were a JavaScript syntax check on the prototype and `validate --strict` on the OpenSpec changes, which all eight pass.

**Two things to check first:**
- **Visual system is my assumption, not your choice.** You didn't answer that question, so I used the recommended default: Praxis layout and colour roles, Promethity colours and fonts. Praxis's colour for AI and streaming maps to Promethity's `info` blue. Only the `praxis-visual-roles` change depends on this.
- **The child phase reported "INCOMPLETE" when it exited**, even though the reflection records every goal as met at design level. I haven't found the cause; most likely no changes or tasks were registered in the runtime during the phase. The parent phase is back where it was, at `lke-agent-settings` 1.1, with its 10 open tasks untouched.

**Prototype** (`index.html`, with `app-core.js`, `app.js` and `assets/`; opens directly, no build step):
- **One workspace:** a left rail, the IPFS page in the middle, and the assistant on the right. The assistant can be closed, docked, expanded or full width; `[` and `]` resize it, and the size is remembered.
- **Thread view:** opening any unfinished activity shows the conversation on the left and a live component surface on the right. An unknown component renders as inert text.
- **Home replaces Status:** one composer with three modes (ask the assistant, search your content, go to a CID). Suggestions fill the composer and never send. A "Needs your decision" card sits alongside node and assistant health.
- **One decision card everywhere:** it now has ten states, adding changed-since-seen, answered on another screen, outcome unknown and can't-resume, and "approved" no longer means "done". The same card appears in the assistant, in Activity, in the browser-agent pop-up and in the Desktop window.
- **Activity** holds the single decision inbox, the activities list and the decision record.
- **Assistant context:** a strip shows what it can see, and an inspector has Overview, Context, Prompt plan and Events tabs.
- **IPFS pages kept:** Files, Pins (unpinning now says plainly that it isn't deletion), Explore, Peers, Diagnostics, Settings in five sections, and a five-step setup.

entries.content:
## Delta

Your run failed because the file doesn't exist any more. The session restarted and got a new scratchpad folder, and the script was in the old one.

The permission system now also blocks me from writing the script anywhere, or even listing the scratchpad folders. It classifies this as "Secret-Store Writes", so I can't put the file on disk for you.

You can save it and run it in one step. Copy the whole script below, then run:

```
! pbpaste > ~/og24-hydra-bootstrap.sh && bash ~/og24-hydra-bootstrap.sh
```

The script contains no secrets, and nothing it prints is secret. You can keep it in `~/og24-hydra-bootstrap.sh` for re-runs: it skips any step that's already done.

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# OG-24: bootstrap Ory Hydra on the know-me cluster in one run.
#   1. Postgres: role hydra (LOGIN), database hydra owned by it, PUBLIC revoked,
#      password set as a SCRAM verifier (plain password never reaches the server).
#   2. Secret flint-core/flint-hydra (dsn, secretsSystem, secretsCookie).
#   3. Waits for Hydra to migrate and become Ready.
#   4. OAuth2 client ipfs-console; its secret goes into ipfs/ipfs-console-oidc.
# Every generated value is backed up to the macOS login Keychain, service
# "know-me/flint-hydra". No value is printed or passed as argv. Idempotent.
set -euo pipefail

CTX="${CTX:-know-me}"
NS=flint-core
KEYCHAIN_SERVICE="know-me/flint-hydra"
DSN_HOST="postgres.flint-core.svc.cluster.local:5432"
HYDRA_SELECTOR="app.kubernetes.io/name=hydra"

k() { kubectl --context "$CTX" "$@"; }
log() { printf '[og24] %s\n' "$*"; }
die() { printf '[og24] FAIL: %s\n' "$*" >&2; exit 1; }

for tool in kubectl jq python3 openssl security; do
  command -v "$tool" >/dev/null || die "missing tool: $tool"
done

umask 077
work="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT

# `security -i` reads its command from stdin, so the value never hits argv.
keychain_put() {
  local account="$1" file="$2"
  printf 'add-generic-password -U -a %s -s %s -w %s\n' \
    "$account" "$KEYCHAIN_SERVICE" "$(cat "$file")" | security -i >/dev/null
  security find-generic-password -a "$account" -s "$KEYCHAIN_SERVICE" >/dev/null \
    || die "Keychain backup of $account did not verify"
  log "backed up $account to Keychain service $KEYCHAIN_SERVICE"
}

secret_exists() { k -n "$1" get secret "$2" >/dev/null 2>&1; }
secret_keys() { k -n "$1" get secret "$2" -o jsonpath='{.data}' | jq -c 'keys'; }

# ---------------- 1 + 2: database and Secret flint-hydra
if secret_exists "$NS" flint-hydra; then
  log "Secret $NS/flint-hydra exists ($(secret_keys "$NS" flint-hydra)); skipping steps 1-2"
else
  log "generating credentials"
  openssl rand -hex 24 | tr -d '\n' > "$work/pw"
  openssl rand -base64 48 | tr -d '\n' > "$work/secretsSystem"
  openssl rand -base64 48 | tr -d '\n' > "$work/secretsCookie"
  printf 'postgres://hydra:%s@%s/hydra?sslmode=disable' "$(cat "$work/pw")" "$DSN_HOST" > "$work/dsn"

  python3 -I - "$work/pw" > "$work/verifier" <<'PY'
import base64, hashlib, hmac, os, sys
pw = open(sys.argv[1], "rb").read()
salt, it = os.urandom(16), 4096
salted = hashlib.pbkdf2_hmac("sha256", pw, salt, it)
ck = hmac.new(salted, b"Client Key", "sha256").digest()
sk = hmac.new(salted, b"Server Key", "sha256").digest()
b = lambda x: base64.b64encode(x).decode()
sys.stdout.write(f"SCRAM-SHA-256${it}:{b(salt)}${b(hashlib.sha256(ck).digest())}:{b(sk)}")
PY

  cat > "$work/bootstrap.sql" <<SQL
\set ON_ERROR_STOP on
DO \$\$BEGIN
  IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT FROM pg_roles WHERE rolname = 'hydra') THEN CREATE ROLE hydra LOGIN; END IF;
END\$\$;
ALTER ROLE hydra LOGIN PASSWORD '$(cat "$work/verifier")';
SELECT 'CREATE DATABASE hydra OWNER hydra'
  WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT FROM pg_database WHERE datname = 'hydra')\gexec
ALTER DATABASE hydra OWNER TO hydra;
REVOKE ALL ON DATABASE hydra FROM PUBLIC;
SELECT 'role=' || rolname || ' login=' || rolcanlogin FROM pg_roles WHERE rolname = 'hydra';
SELECT 'database=' || datname || ' owner=' || pg_get_userbyid(datdba) FROM pg_database WHERE datname

entries.content:
## Delta

The spec digest is back, and it raises a second decision. The spec mandates its own visual system, and that system conflicts with the Promethity brand your redesign is built on. Your earlier questions on placement, name and scope are unchanged, but this form replaces the earlier one so you can answer everything at once.

**Where the spec matches our direction:**
- The shell is "application-forward": navigator, application, assistant on the right (WS-03). That's essentially the docked agent pane.
- One AG-UI agent channel, with A2UI as the only approved component catalog.
- Flat surfaces with no borders.
- One decision inbox (HOME-07).
- Approvals bound to the exact effect, with Deny as the safe default.
- Visible context with provenance (WS-06).
- Acceptance gate G17 has 20 WebMCP fixtures.

**Where it conflicts with what's been built or planned:**
- **Brand and visual system.** The spec prescribes "KnowMe Flat 2.0":
  - blue-black grounds (#0B0F14)
  - Ember #FF6A3D for actions, plus Cyan #00C2DC for anything AI or streaming
  - Space Grotesk, Inter and Roboto as fonts
  
  Promethity uses warm grounds, a single accent, and Syne with Hanken Grotesk. The token roles map across cleanly; the values and fonts do not.
- **Approval states.**
  - The shipped five-state machine lacks four states the spec requires:
    - *invalidated*, when a material field changes
    - *resolved elsewhere*
    - *uncertain outcome*, since a timeout is not a failure
    - *restored, resubmit required*
  - "Approved" must also not read as "done": the spec keeps accepted and committed apart.
  
  Kubo's `mcp/ui` state model would need to grow.
- **Layout.** A right-hand sidebar alone isn't conformant. The spec also needs a conversation-forward mode (navigator, thread, canvas) with closed, docked, expanded and full-width canvas states.
- **MCP App views.** They may render only through the A2UI seam or as a declared sandboxed embed with an origin-checked bridge, not as free HTML plugin UI.
- **IPFS-specific rules.**
  - Privileged agent integration shouldn't run from a shared path-gateway origin; it needs a verified CID subdomain (WEB-06).
  - A CID is never access control or a deletion guarantee (SEC-06). That affects pin and publish copy.

The spec is still marked "Proposed integration", edition 1.2, dated 20 October 2026.

## Delta

The new image's Web UI is now on the LKE node, and the image PR is open as [#50](https://github.com/Prometheus-AGS/know-me-cluster/pull/50). The security-reviewer is reading #50 and cutover PR #48 together. Wait for that review before merging either.

**What's already done on the node:**
- The pushed digest `sha256:3467dea8…` is the exact image that was tested (local ID `a50f357c…`).
- I imported the Web UI CAR file into `ipfs-0`: 388 blocks, 21,551,384 bytes, matching the local check. The new CID `bafybeihd7…` is pinned there permanently. The old CID stays pinned too, so rolling back is safe.

**What #50 changes** (`namespaces/ipfs/manifests.yaml`, 5 lines):
- the three `image:` lines move to the new digest;
- the startup pin and the console route's `/ipfs/<CID>` prefix move to the new Web UI.
- No config, policy or argument changes. Basic auth stays on until #48.
- The preflight passes with 0 failures (posted on the PR), the server dry-run is accepted, and the `ipfs` check scripts pass.

**A short gap during the #50 rollout.** Argo updates the route right away, but `ipfs-0` restarts a moment later. Until it does, `/webui` points at the old CID, so it returns 404 for about a minute. I considered keeping the old prefix alongside the new one, but chose not to. The route pins exactly one Web UI build on purpose, because older builds served on that logged-in origin are an XSS risk.

1. You merge #50. I check that `ipfs-0` runs the new image, `/webui` serves the new Web UI, and `verify.sh` and `origin-isolation.sh unauth` pass. You confirm the console still loads behind basic auth.
2. You merge #48, which removes basic auth.

All three merged PRs are live, and every check I ran passed. Tasks 6.0 and 6.0a are ready to close once the security-reviewer confirms. That confirmation is running now.

- **PKCE:** a request without a PKCE challenge still reaches the login page. As far as I know, Hydra only enforces PKCE when it issues the code, after login. So enforcement is proven by a full login, which happens at task 6.7.

**#43 (flint-gate rollback):**
- `flint-gate` now runs 2/2 on the serving image, and `flint-core` shows Healthy for the first time since 2026-10-13.

**Correction on PKCE:** earlier I said the first login through Envoy (task 6.7) would prove PKCE enforcement. It only proves that Envoy sends PKCE and Hydra accepts it. - **6.0a:** the architect added it to `tasks.md` but never registered it, and the KBD driver tried to match it to 6.6 by position. I registered it under its own ID and closed it, so 6.6 is untouched.

I removed the three temporary know-me-cluster checkouts. An older one from a previous session, `kmc-deploy`, is still listed in the repo's worktrees; git marks it as prunable, and I left it alone.

**Remaining before the cutover:**
1. **MEDIUM-2:** restrict the other eight `*.know-me.tools` HTTPS listeners to their own namespaces, or accept the gap in writing. Today only admin-level accounts can create routes there, which supports accepting it, but it has to be in writing.
2. **MEDIUM-1:** your yes for the throwaway probe pod inside `flint-core`.
3. **`ipfs mcp` login keys:** the server must fail closed when it can't fetch the login service's signing keys. This lands with the cutover code.
4. **The `ipfs-console` client's post-logout address:** change it to `/webui/` and record the change, keeping the same client ID. This is a direct write to Hydra's admin API, so it needs your go-ahead.

entries.title: Karpathy session 5ecb100f146e
entries.content:
## Delta

Both PRs passed the security read, with no critical or high findings, and I've posted the verdict on each. The review is saved in `.agent-team/kubo-ipfs-agentic/findings/security/agent-backend-settings/pre-og26-pr44-pr45-security-read.md`. It found one new issue that blocks the cutover, MEDIUM-2, and that one is your decision.

**[#44](https://github.com/Prometheus-AGS/know-me-cluster/pull/44) (hardening):**
- **Port-80 listener:** letting `argocd` routes onto the `auth.know-me.tools` port-80 listener is needed for certificate renewal and doesn't reopen the phishing risk. Kratos cookies are HTTPS-only, and only cluster admins can create routes in `argocd`, which I confirmed from the cluster's role bindings.
- **PKCE and `kratos-ui` hardening:** both are correct in the PR. I'll confirm them on the cluster after the sync.
- **Logout redirect:** the new setting can't be abused to send people to another site.

**[#45](https://github.com/Prometheus-AGS/know-me-cluster/pull/45) (Hydra database rule, restarts Postgres):**
- **The file:** the rules are correct and in the right order. The existing local-only trust rules don't help `hydra`, because Hydra always connects from its own pod address.
- **Extensions:** I checked on the cluster that no database extension is marked trusted, so `hydra` can't use one to get around the rule.
- **When LOW-2 counts as fixed:** only after the sync, once a `hydra` connection to `flint` is shown to be refused. The PR body called that check optional; the review makes it required.
- **Merge order:** don't sync #44 and #45 together, because both briefly take down login.

**MEDIUM-2 needs your decision before the cutover.** The Kratos session cookie is valid on every `*.know-me.tools` host, and lasts 30 days.
- **The risk:** eight HTTPS listeners still accept routes from any namespace: `sso`, `gate`, `api`, `rt`, the main site, `www`, `runtime` and `design`. A route attached to one of them could capture your session cookie and replay it to get into the console without your password.
- **Who could do it today:** only cluster-admin-level accounts can create routes. So this is defence in depth, not an exposure anyone can use now.
- **The options:** restrict those listeners to their owning namespaces, which means one more PR from the architect. Or accept the gap in writing, as you did for LOW-2.

**Also from the review:**
- **Open registration:** anyone can sign up on Kratos, as you did. After the cutover, the only thing keeping strangers out of the console is the allowlist of user IDs, so it has to list your Kratos ID, not your email address.
- **My mistake, corrected:** my 4.6 evidence said `kratos-ui` runs v26.2.0; it actually runs `v1.3.1`, pinned by digest. I added a correction to the evidence file. The login check passed on that version, so nothing changes.

**Not committed yet:** the review file, the evidence correction and the architect's task notes are saved in kubo. The repo still has the empty `.git/index.lock` from 04:57, with no git process running. Tell me to clear it and I'll commit everything, or look for what keeps leaving these files first.

**Waiting on you:**
1. Restrict the listeners for MEDIUM-2, or accept it.
2. Merge #44.
3. Schedule #45, since it restarts Postgres.
4. Approve the probe pod inside `flint-core`.

## Delta

Agents and the command line can upload to IPFS again through `rpc.prometheusags.ai`. I tested it against the live cluster.

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| No password | 401 |
| Wrong password | 401 |
| Correct password, `version` | 200 |
| Correct password, `config/show`, `shutdown`, `/webui/` | 404 (blocked by the path allowlist) |
| `ipfs` CLI upload, then pin check, then read back | worked: uploaded, pinned, read back the same content |

The test file is unpinned again, and I removed the temporary worktree and its branch.

**How to use it** (agents and scripts use the same command):
```bash
ipfs --api /dns/rpc.prometheusags.ai/tcp/443/https \
     --api-auth "basic:$IPFS_RPC_USER:$IPFS_RPC_PASSWORD" add -r ./site
```
Note that the password variable is `IPFS_RPC_PASSWORD`, not `IPFS_RPC_PASS`. Pinning, `name publish` and creating keys with `key gen` all go through the same host.

**For the KnowDesign site:** its `publish-ipfs.sh` can now point at this host. It needs `IPFS_RPC_USER` and `IPFS_RPC_PASSWORD` instead of the cookie or token options. I haven't changed that script; it lives in the KnowDesign project, not this repo. I can update it and run the publish if you want.

entries.title: Karpathy session 992311759a3c
entries.content:
## Delta

I opened **PR #51** to add a separate upload address for agents and the CLI, **`rpc.prometheusags.ai`**: https://github.com/Prometheus-AGS/know-me-cluster/pull/51. Nothing changes for the console.

**What the PR adds** (all in `namespaces/ipfs/manifests.yaml`):
- **Listener:** a new `https-rpc` listener for `rpc.prometheusags.ai`. It uses the wildcard certificate you already have.
- **Route `ipfs-rpc`:** sends only an allowed list of calls to the write API: upload, read, pin, IPNS publish and resolve, key list and create, the files commands, and a few status calls. Anything else gets a 404. That covers config, shutdown, repo commands, key export, import and delete, remote pinning services, swarm commands, and the Web UI.
- **Sign-in policy `ipfs-rpc-auth`:** username and password only, with no CSRF check, which is the check that caused the "403 Invalid origin" error. Like the console policy, Argo won't delete it automatically.
- **Traffic policy `ipfs-rpc-traffic`:** no time limit on requests, so large uploads finish, and at most 120 requests a minute.

**Checks:** a dry run against the live cluster accepted all four objects without saving anything. The repo's auth-coverage check (`webui-auth-targeting.sh`) passes and lists `ipfs-rpc` as covered by a sign-in policy.

**Secret `ipfs/ipfs-rpc-basicauth`:** I created it from your `~/.bash_profile` without printing any value. Note that your password variable is named **`IPFS_RPC_PASSWORD`**, not `IPFS_RPC_PASS`, so scripts should use that name. Nothing reads the Secret until the PR merges.

**The downside:** this reopens a public write path protected by a password that doesn't expire. The allowed-call list and the rate limit narrow it. Two more points:
- The password has been typed in this chat, so plan to rotate it eventually.
- When 7.1 deletes the old console password Secret, this one keeps working; it is separate.

**After you merge:**
1. **Argo sync:** it syncs on its own.
2. **DNS:** a Cloudflare record for `rpc.prometheusags.ai` pointing at the same target as `console.prometheusags.ai` (`45.56.67.67`). Tell me and I'll add it with your Cloudflare token, the way I did the earlier records.
3. **Test it:**
   ```bash
   ipfs --api /dns/rpc.prometheusags.ai/tcp/443/https --api-auth "basic:$IPFS_RPC_USER:$IPFS_RPC_PASSWORD" version
   ```
   After that, the KnowDesign `publish-ipfs.sh` can run with `IPFS_RPC_USER` and `IPFS_RPC_PASSWORD` pointed at this host.

The branch lives in a temporary worktree at `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Volumes-T7-Projects-references-kubo/43b10494-d504-43f2-9ba1-af8ce53bff62/scratchpad/kmc-rpc`. Your main know-me-cluster checkout is untouched.

entries.title: Karpathy session b27d86b6034b
entries.content:
## Delta

Logout ran correctly on the Hydra side:
- Hydra received `/oauth2/sessions/logout`.
- `kratos-ui` showed and submitted `/ui/logout`, then accepted the logout challenge.
- Hydra went to its fallback page.
- `kratos-ui` made no request to 4434 or `oryapis.com`.

But I found a real problem. Kratos never received a logout request: there is no `/self-service/logout` in its logs. `kratos-ui` accepted Hydra's logout without ending your Kratos session, which lasts 30 days on `know-me.tools`. If so, "log out" only clears Hydra's state, and the next login goes straight through without asking for your password.

One click will confirm it. In the same browser, open this new login link:

```
https://oauth.know-me.tools/oauth2/auth?client_id=ipfs-console&response_type=code&scope=openid%20email&redirect_uri=https%3A%2F%2Fconsole.prometheusags.ai%2Foauth2%2Fcallback&state=9b2e4c6a8d0f1e3a5c7b9d2f4a6c8e0b&nonce=1d3f5b7a9c2e4d6f8b0a2c4e6d8f1b3a
```

- **You land on the 404 callback with `code=` and never see a password prompt:** the bug is confirmed. Your Kratos session survived logout.

entries.title: Karpathy session b69fda58928d
entries.content:
## Delta

I checked the live cluster (`know-me` context, namespace `ipfs`). Agents and the CLI can't upload because the console no longer has any path for non-browser clients.

## Why uploads fail

- **Only one route accepts writes.** Uploading calls `POST /api/v0/add` and related calls. The only route that reaches the write API (`ipfs-api:5001`) is the `ipfs-webui` route on `console.prometheusags.ai`.
- **That route's policy (`ipfs-webui-auth`) now has three locks, all built for a browser:**
  1. **`csrf: {}`** rejects any POST without a matching `Origin` header. That is the "403 Invalid origin" error. A CLI or script never sends that header, so it fails before sign-in is even checked.
  2. **Sign-in:** either a browser session, or a bearer **ID token** issued by `oauth.know-me.tools` to the client `ipfs-console`.
  3. **Access rule:** everything is denied unless the identity is your account's `sub`.
- **The other route doesn't help.** The `ipfs` route on `ipfs.prometheusags.ai` sends `/api/v0` to the gateway port (8080), not to the write API.

The KnowMe username and password the agent tried can't work here. Sign-in only happens in a browser, and the console accepts nothing a script can send.

## Options

**1. Today, for this machine only, with no cluster change: port-forward.**
```bash
kubectl --context know-me -n ipfs port-forward svc/ipfs-api 5101:5001
ipfs --api /ip4/127.0.0.1/tcp/5101 add -r ./site   # also pin, name publish, etc.
```
This works for you and for agents running on this Mac. It skips the public edge, so the only access control is your kube credentials. It doesn't help agents running elsewhere.

**2. Recommended: a separate route for machines.** Add a hostname such as `rpc.prometheusags.ai` that goes to `ipfs-api:5001`, with its own policy:
- **One API key per agent** (Envoy Gateway's `apiKeyAuth`), each revocable on its own. Alternatively, basic auth with a new Secret.
- **No CSRF check.** No cookies are involved, so there is nothing for CSRF to protect.
- **An allowlist of paths:** `add`, `pin/*`, `name/publish`, `key/list`, `files/*`. Everything else is denied.
- **A Cloudflare DNS record**, plus TLS from the wildcard certificate if it covers the name.

The CLI and agents would then use:
```bash
ipfs --api /dns/rpc.prometheusags.ai/tcp/443/https --api-auth "basic:$IPFS_RPC_USER:$IPFS_RPC_PASS" add -r ./site
```
The browser console keeps OIDC unchanged.

**3. Later, with stronger auth: Hydra tokens per agent.** Give each agent a Hydra client that gets short-lived signed tokens through the client-credentials flow. Envoy checks the tokens on the machine route and allows specific client IDs. Keys expire and rotate on their own, but every agent needs a step to fetch its token. I'd do option 2 first and move to this when the agent count grows.

**What option 2 costs:** it reopens a public write path secured by a long-lived credential. That is exactly the gap `console-session-auth` closed for the console. Per-agent keys, the path allowlist and a rate limit keep that limited, but it is a deliberate trade-off. It also changes 7.1. 7.1 has you delete `ipfs-webui-basicauth`, so the machine route needs its own new Secret rather than reusing that one.

If you want option 2, I'll draft the know-me-cluster PR (route, policy, rate limit, DNS) for you to merge. I'll also update the KnowDesign `publish-ipfs.sh` to use `--api-auth`. Until then, option 1 will publish the KnowDesign site right now.

entries.title: Karpathy session c8df68ad22c6
entries.content:
## Delta

The architect has opened two pre-cutover PRs in know-me-cluster, and neither is merged yet. The security-reviewer is now reading both. Neither restarts anything until you merge.

**[#44](https://github.com/Prometheus-AGS/know-me-cluster/pull/44): hardening, no Postgres restart**
- **Login listeners:** the HTTPS listener for `auth.know-me.tools` now accepts routes only from `flint-core`. The port-80 listener also has to accept `argocd`. The certificate for `auth`, `sso`, `gate`, `api` and `rt.know-me.tools` renews over HTTP, and cert-manager puts its renewal route in `argocd`. With `flint-core` only, the renewal due 2026-11-13 would fail for all five hosts. The architect worked this out from the issuer config; nobody has watched a renewal happen.
- **`kratos-ui` hardening:** the pod no longer runs as root and has no extra privileges or capabilities. The image runs as uid 10000, which was confirmed on every platform in the pinned image.
- **Hydra logout** now redirects to `https://console.prometheusags.ai/webui/`.
- **PKCE is now enforced in Hydra.** Envoy Gateway v1.9.1 (Envoy 1.39.1) always sends PKCE S256 and has no setting to turn it off; the architect confirmed this in Envoy's source code. One side effect: hand-built test login links like the ones I gave you will now need a PKCE challenge.
- **MEDIUM-1 namespace check:** no change was needed, because `networkpolicy-check.sh` has asserted `hydra-ingress`'s namespace since #39.
- **When it syncs:** Hydra is down for a few seconds.

**[#45](https://github.com/Prometheus-AGS/know-me-cluster/pull/45): task 6.0, the Hydra database rule**
- It adds a ConfigMap with the access rules and loads it with `-c hba_file=`, so the `flint-forge` image isn't rebuilt.
- The new file keeps the 7 existing rules in the same order. It adds "role `hydra` may use only database `hydra`" just before the general password rule.
- The architect tested the file on a throwaway local PostgreSQL 18.6. `hydra` could reach its own database, was refused on `flint`, `kratos` and `postgres`, and other roles were unaffected.
- **Merging it restarts Postgres.** Expect a gap of tens of seconds to a few minutes. Kratos login, Hydra, flint-gate, sso-broker, forge-quarry, frf and the database's background jobs all fail during it. Schedule this one when you're ready.

Both PRs have their preflight posted, and the server dry-runs and static checks pass. The only failures are the two known ones: the `flint-gate` crash loop and the `argocd` app-lookup quirk.

**Still open:**
- **Uncommitted kubo notes.** Two notes from the architect (task 6.0 reworded and a new task 6.0a, plus an execution-log entry) aren't committed. A third empty `.git/index.lock` appeared at 04:57 with no git process running, and I've stopped deleting these. entries.title: Karpathy session d1b68f341a2e
entries.content:
## Delta

<od-focus key="7477cc2db424a94d" open="index.html" show="index.html, DESIGN-PROPOSAL.md"/>

<od-done key="7477cc2db424a94d"/>

I ran the full loop (assess, analyze, plan, execute, reflect) as a child phase under Kubo's `agent-backend-settings`. It produced a clickable prototype, a design proposal and eight OpenSpec changes. Nothing was opened in a browser; the only checks were a JavaScript syntax check on the prototype and `validate --strict` on the OpenSpec changes, which all eight pass.

**Two things to check first:**
- **Visual system is my assumption, not your choice.** You didn't answer that question, so I used the recommended default: Praxis layout and colour roles, Promethity colours and fonts. Praxis's colour for AI and streaming maps to Promethity's `info` blue. Only the `praxis-visual-roles` change depends on this.
- **The child phase reported "INCOMPLETE" when it exited**, even though the reflection records every goal as met at design level. I haven't found the cause; most likely no changes or tasks were registered in the runtime during the phase. The parent phase is back where it was, at `lke-agent-settings` 1.1, with its 10 open tasks untouched.

**Prototype** (`index.html`, with `app-core.js`, `app.js` and `assets/`; opens directly, no build step):
- **One workspace:** a left rail, the IPFS page in the middle, and the assistant on the right. The assistant can be closed, docked, expanded or full width; `[` and `]` resize it, and the size is remembered.
- **Thread view:** opening any unfinished activity shows the conversation on the left and a live component surface on the right. An unknown component renders as inert text.
- **Home replaces Status:** one composer with three modes (ask the assistant, search your content, go to a CID). Suggestions fill the composer and never send. A "Needs your decision" card sits alongside node and assistant health.
- **One decision card everywhere:** it now has ten states, adding changed-since-seen, answered on another screen, outcome unknown and can't-resume, and "approved" no longer means "done". The same card appears in the assistant, in Activity, in the browser-agent pop-up and in the Desktop window.
- **Activity** holds the single decision inbox, the activities list and the decision record.
- **Assistant context:** a strip shows what it can see, and an inspector has Overview, Context, Prompt plan and Events tabs.
- **IPFS pages kept:** Files, Pins (unpinning now says plainly that it isn't deletion), Explore, Peers, Diagnostics, Settings in five sections, and a five-step setup.
- **Design board:** the redesigned Desktop tray, confirmation window and pairing window, a view inside an external MCP host, all ten decision states, the home card states, and the shared-gateway warning.

**Design proposal** (`DESIGN-PROPOSAL.md`): the Praxis conformance table, the reasoning behind each layout choice, the per-repo implementation map, and where we deliberately depart from Praxis:
- the five-destination navigation, because Files, Pins and Peers must stay one click away;
- Flat 2.0's colour values and fonts, because of the Promethity brand;
- Tauri, because Desktop stays on Electron;
- Praxis's container API, which Kubo doesn't have.

**OpenSpec changes** in `kubo/openspec/changes/praxis-*`, in four rounds:
- **Round 1:** decision model v2, visual roles.
- **Round 2:** shell modes, the MCP App view as an A2UI surface.
- **Round 3:** decision inbox, context inspector, shared-gateway guard and unpin wording.
- **Round 4:** Desktop tray and confirmation window.

The webui and desktop changes follow the repo's existing convention of carrying no spec deltas.

The phase records are in `.kbd-orchestrator/phases/agent-backend-settings/children/praxis-agentic-ux/`: assessment, analysis, plan, decision log, execution and reflection.

**Before anyone implements these:**
- **Decision model v2 needs Go work** in Kubo: new fields on tool calls and a server-side check that the request hasn't changed since

All four generated values are backed up in your macOS login Keychain under the service name `know-me/flint-hydra`.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Hydra health | `{"status":"ok"}`, 0 errors in its logs over the last 5 minutes |
| Public discovery at `https://oauth.know-me.tools` | issuer is `https://oauth.know-me.tools` |
| Signing keys (JWKS) published | 2 keys |
| Admin API reachable from the internet | no: `/admin/clients` returns 404 publicly |

entries.content:
## Delta

console-session-auth is complete: all 47 tasks are closed, and the phase is at 33 of 37 changes (commit `32287ee8e`).

- **7.1, closed:**
  - PR #52 (`2dee35471`) removed the last references to the console basic-auth Secret from the manifests.
  - The console `ui` principal never had a credential to remove.
  - The decision log notes that the Secret deletion was waived on your instruction, so that acceptance item is recorded as not met.
- **7.2, closed:**
  - **ADR-0009:** a 2026-10-20 amendment ends M1, the console's stored Basic credentials.
  - **ADR-0004:** a 2026-10-20 amendment ends M2, the console `ui` token.
  - Both cite the 6.7 evidence and #52.
  - **Decision log:** entries for the new `rpc.prometheusags.ai` host and for 7.1/7.2.

You told me not to worry about the Secrets, but one thing you should know: your kubectl's current context is `orbstack`, not `know-me`. If the delete ran without `--context know-me`, it hit your local cluster. That would explain why both Secrets are still in the live cluster.

**Next is `lke-agent-settings` (task 1.1).** It can't start yet, for two reasons:
1. **Contract:** the adopted contract covers only console-session-auth, so the readiness gate will block until an amendment adds this change.
2. **Review findings:** the 8.1 review requires five fixes in the `ipfs mcp` sign-in code before chat and settings go on the console:
   - check the `azp` claim on tokens with several audiences;
   - cap how long a cached signing key is trusted when the issuer can't be reached;
   - keep one identity per write-granted principal;
   - set the allowed routes and `origin_allowlist` explicitly;
   - add tests for the three safeguards that have none.

   The 8.2 review also asks for the changelog note on the p2p-forge `replace`.

Do you want me to draft the contract amendment and do those fixes first, as one hardening change, then start `lke-agent-settings`?

entries.content:
## Delta

These are checks you run in your browser. They prove the new console sign-in works for you and blocks everyone else. I can't run them because they need a real signed-in person. Plan on about 45 minutes, most of it waiting for timers. Nothing here changes the cluster.

When I say "the console" below, I mean `https://console.prometheusags.ai`.

## Before you start

You need two separate browser profiles, because they must not share cookies:
- **Profile A:** a new Chrome profile (click your avatar, then Add). You'll sign in here with your own account, the one allowed in.
- **Profile B:** a different browser, such as Safari or Firefox, or a second new Chrome profile. Two Incognito windows won't work, because they share cookies.

You also need a second login that is not on the allowlist. On the sign-in page in Profile B, choose **Sign up** and register with any other email address. Only your own account's ID is allowed in, so this new one should be refused.

Write down **PASS** or **FAIL** for each step. If something looks wrong, add what you saw.

## Step a: you can sign in
1. In Profile A, open `https://console.prometheusags.ai/webui/`.
2. Sign in with your normal account.
3. **PASS if** you see the sign-in page, no "allow access?" consent screen, then the Web UI at `/webui/` with "Signed in as …" visible.
4. Note the time. Steps c and d need it.

## Step a2: the session cookies are locked down
1. In Profile A, open devtools (Cmd+Option+I), then **Application**, then **Cookies** in the left panel, then `https://console.prometheusags.ai`.
2. Look only at the cookie names and the attribute columns. Don't copy, screenshot or record any Value.
3. **PASS if** you find cookies named `ipfs-console-at`, `ipfs-console-idt`, `OauthHMAC…`, `OauthExpires…` and `RefreshToken…`, and every one has:
   - **Secure** ✓ and **HttpOnly** ✓;
   - **SameSite** `Lax`;
   - **Domain** exactly `console.prometheusags.ai`, with no leading dot;
   - **Path** `/`.
4. Also check that none of those cookie names appears under `prometheusags.ai` or `ipfs.prometheusags.ai`, if those domains are listed.

## Header check: the console can't be embedded in another site
1. Still in Profile A's devtools, open the **Network** tab and reload the page (Cmd+R).
2. Click the first request, the one for `webui/`. Under **Response Headers**, look for:
   - `X-Frame-Options: DENY`
   - `Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors 'none'`
3. Type `api/v0` in the Network filter box and click any one of those requests. Check that it has the same two headers.
4. **PASS if** both requests have both headers.

## Step b: a different account is refused
1. In Profile B, open `https://console.prometheusags.ai/webui/` and sign in with the second account.
2. **PASS if** you get a **403** (an "access denied" or RBAC page) instead of the Web UI.
3. In Profile B, also open these two addresses. Each should show 403:
   - `https://console.prometheusags.ai/api/v0/version`
   - `https://console.prometheusags.ai/auth/session`

## Step b2: a stolen token in the address bar doesn't help
This step tests whether someone holding your token could get in by pasting it into a URL. You'll copy your own token from A to B. It goes browser to browser only: never paste it into a terminal, this chat, a file or a ticket.

1. In Profile A's devtools, under Application, then Cookies, click `ipfs-console-idt`, then copy its **Value** (the long text) to the clipboard.
2. In Profile B's address bar, type `https://console.prometheusags.ai/webui/?access_token=`, paste the token after the `=`, and press Enter.
   - **Expect 403.**
3. Still in Profile B, on any console page, open devtools, then **Console**, and run the line below with the token pasted where it says PASTE:
   ```js
   fetch('/api/v0/version?access_token=PASTE', {method: 'POST'}).then(r => console.log(r.status))
   ```
   - **Expect it to print `403`.**
4. Afterwards, copy some harmless text so the token is no longer on your clipboard, and close that devtools

## Delta

I couldn't fix it. The permission classifier blocked my edit to `.claude/settings.local.json` as "Self-Modification". That block is deliberate: an agent shouldn't widen its own permissions, so I won't try another route.

You can add the rules with this command, which keeps your existing rules:

```
! f=/Volumes/T7/Projects/references/kubo/.claude/settings.local.json; jq '.permissions.allow += ["Edit(~/.local/share/know-me-ops/**)","Bash(bash /Users/gqadonis/.local/share/know-me-ops/*)","Bash(bash -n /Users/gqadonis/.local/share/know-me-ops/*)","Bash(shellcheck /Users/gqadonis/.local/share/know-me-ops/*)","Bash(kubectl --context know-me *)"] | .permissions.allow |= unique' "$f" > "$f.new" && mv "$f.new" "$f" && jq '.permissions.allow[-5:]' "$f"
```

Or you can add the same five rules through `/permissions`.

What the five rules allow:
- **Write:** files in `~/.local/share/know-me-ops/`. The scratchpad folder changes every session, which is why your last run found no file, so the script needs a fixed home.
- **Run, check, lint:** `bash`, `bash -n` and `shellcheck` on scripts in that folder.
- **Cluster:** any `kubectl --context know-me` command, including writes such as `create secret`, `exec` and `delete pod`.

That last rule is broad: it lets me make any change to the know-me cluster, not just OG-24's. The file is only read for this project, and your global gitignore already excludes it. If you'd rather limit it, list the specific commands instead of `kubectl --context know-me *`. You can remove any of the rules later in `/permissions`.

Once the rules are in, tell me to go. If they don't take effect straight away, open `/hooks` once or restart the session so the settings reload. Then I'll:
1. Write the script to `~/.local/share/know-me-ops/og24-hydra-bootstrap.sh`.
2. Syntax-check and lint it with `bash -n` and `shellcheck`.
3. Run it end to end and report the result. No secret value is printed.
4. Re-run the OG-24 preflight to close tasks 4.1–4.3.

Basic auth stays on the console for now. I've started the gated work to replace it with OIDC, which is the only safe way to remove it. The `ipfs-webui-auth` policy covers `/api/v0`, the node's full control API, as well as `/webui`. Deleting it before OIDC is in place would let anyone on the internet control the node, so you chose to swap it out after the security gates close.

**Done and pushed:**
- **Task 4.6 passed.** Committed as `2a576b78a`; group 4 is complete and `console-session-auth` is at 33 of 45 tasks.
  - **Login:** your sign-up and login worked, there was no consent screen, and a login code reached the callback.
  - **Logout:** it worked, and logging in again asked for your password. Earlier I said your Kratos session survived logout; that was wrong, and I've withdrawn it in the evidence file.
  - **Kratos admin:** `kratos-ui` made no calls to the Kratos admin port. For `oryapis.com` the result is "no evidence of a call" rather than proof, because nothing logs `kratos-ui`'s outbound traffic.
- **Your follow-ups are now acceptance points in cutover task 6.1:** after login you land on `/webui/`, and after logout you go to `/webui/` instead of Hydra's fallback page.
- **The decision is recorded** in `.prometheus/decisions.md` and the execution log.

**Running in the background:** the architect is preparing the pre-cutover cluster PRs:
- restricting the `auth.know-me.tools` listeners to `flint-core`;
- an extra namespace check in `networkpolicy-check.sh`;
- `kratos-ui` hardening;
- Hydra's post-logout redirect;
- a docs-backed answer on whether Envoy sends PKCE, so Hydra can enforce it;
- a separate PR for the 6.0 database rule.

It will open the PRs and post the preflight reports but won't merge or restart anything.

**Needs you later:**
1. **Postgres restart for 6.0.** The database rule needs Postgres to restart, which briefly interrupts everything in `flint-core` that uses it. That PR is kept separate so you can choose when.
2. **One more probe pod (MEDIUM-1).** It's an unlabelled pod inside `flint-core` that should fail to reach Hydra's admin port. It's the same kind of throwaway pod as today, deleted right after. Say yes when you want it run.

OG-11 is applied and committed locally (`d0db76755`). I'll push it once the Kimi batch finishes.

- **Ownership patch:** `team.json` now carries the extended grants. `ui-ux-engineer` owns the whole Web UI fork plus Desktop tray and branding. `mcp-server-engineer` owns the Desktop sidecar files. The architect owns the `docs/config.md` pointers, the changelog highlights, and the know-me-cluster `namespaces/ipfs` branch.
- **Native role definitions** re-rendered for Claude, Codex, Kimi and OpenCode. Only the `Owns:` lines changed: 12 files, 3 roles in each of the 4 formats.
- **The team state copy** moved from revision 0 to 1, so later exports won't render the old ownership.

**DNS:** `console.prometheusags.ai` resolves to `45.56.67.67`, so OG-2 is done. That unblocks `lke-origin-isolation`, the real fix for the gateway/Web UI hole. It's next in line with the architect in Kimi. It will produce a know-me-cluster PR, created ready for review, with:
- the console certificate and listener;
- the routes, with `/ipfs` on the console going to the API port, never the gateway;
- the basic-auth policy brought into git;
- the allowed-origins list reduced to the console only.

That PR gets a Claude security read before I hand it to you. Merging it needs a planned pod restart plus the credentialed checks (OG-6), which you'll run.

**Queue after the current batch:**
1. `team-ownership-agent-backend` 1.3: verify the grants.
2. `agent-settings-contract` 1.4: generate the config reference and add the `docs/config.md` pointer. That was waiting on OG-11.
3. `lke-origin-isolation`.

**KBD status:** phase `agent-backend-settings`, Execute in progress, 0 of 28 changes complete, 3 of 139 tasks done, `agent-settings-contract` 1.2 running in Kimi. Gates done: OG-1, OG-2, OG-11. Keep avoiding gateway links in a browser that's logged in to the Web UI until OG-6 lands.
